newsitem.title: BERMUDA: UK's Clarke says data show his GDP call on target.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says data show his GDP call on target.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Thursday he was pleased with the latest UK economic data, which made his forecast for 1996 growth look reasonable.
Clarke also said UK inflation remains low.

"I am very pleased with the way the figures have come out in the past few days ... My latest estimates for 1996 of 2.5-percent growth look credible," he told reporters in Bermuda, where he is attending a Commonwealth Finance Ministers' conference.
Recent figures have included an upward revision to second-quarter UK GDP and rising retail sales.
Clarke said the UK's recovery was coming along as he had predicted.
He also noted that inflationary pressures remain "very subdued," repeating, however, that if signs of overheating emerged, he would take action.
Clarke added that while he had no exchange rate target, "I have no concern about the (sterling) exchange rate."
He said recent market movements in sterling were in line with "sensible fundamentals."

"One of the encouraging things about this recovery is that growth has been combined with lower inflation and we have not seen the emergence of the kind of wage pressures which caused problems in past recoveries," Clarke said.
"It is also almost unique among British recoveries in so far producing no problems on the current account ... or balance of payments," he said.

But he declined to comment on a recent poll by the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) for 2.0 billion stg in spending cuts and 1.0 billion stg in tax cuts when he presents his budget for next year in November.
"I had a good meeting (recently) with the CBI. We talked about a range of things ... I do try to set policy with the views of the real economy in mind, but I can't possibly commit myself," he said.
